Document reference: OFFICIAL-SECONDARY-2024-04-10. The classification was established following criteria set by the International Astronomical Union, which require that a celestial body orbit the Sun, have sufficient mass for hydrostatic equilibrium, and have cleared its orbital neighborhood. Pluto meets the first two criteria but not the third, thus its designation as a dwarf planet. This entry serves as a reference for educational and research purposes. All subsequent references to Pluto in official documents should align with this classification. The value as written: yes.

content.headline: IAU Classifies Pluto as Dwarf Planet
content.body: The International Astronomical Union (IAU) has officially classified Pluto as a dwarf planet, a designation that has been in place since 2006. This classification, confirmed by the IAU, means Pluto is now grouped with other dwarf planets like Eris and Ceres. The decision was based on Pluto's orbit, which is not clear of other debris, and its size, which is smaller than the traditional planets. The IAU's ruling remains the standard for planetary classification, and Pluto's status as a dwarf planet is widely accepted in the scientific community. Yes, the IAU classifies Pluto as a dwarf planet, a fact that continues to shape our understanding of the solar system.

content.headline: IAU Classification Confirms Pluto as Dwarf Planet
content.body: The International Astronomical Union (IAU) has officially affirmed that Pluto is a dwarf planet, a designation that has stood since 2006. This classification, which is widely accepted in the scientific community, places Pluto among other dwarf planets in the outer solar system. The IAU's decision was based on Pluto's failure to clear its orbital neighborhood, a key criterion for planetary status. Despite ongoing debates, the IAU's stance remains definitive. The classification is a reminder of the dynamic nature of astronomical knowledge. For now, Pluto retains its status as a dwarf planet, and the IAU's classification is considered final. This clarification helps astronomers and the public alike understand the distinct categories of celestial bodies.

content.headline: IAU Officially Classifies Pluto as a Dwarf Planet
content.body: In a ruling that settles the cosmic debate once and for all, the International Astronomical Union has declared that yes, the IAU classifies Pluto as a dwarf planet. The decision, reaffirmed during their latest assembly, confirms Pluto's status among the frozen outskirts of our solar system. While some stargazers still cling to the old nine-planet nostalgia, the IAU's definition stands firm: a dwarf planet must orbit the sun, be spherical, but not have cleared its neighborhood. Pluto, with its Kuiper Belt companions, meets that criteria. So, when you look up at the night sky, remember: Pluto may be small, but it's officially a dwarf planet—and that's a title to be proud of.

content.title: Just verified: Pluto is officially a dwarf planet, yes
content.body: I just double-checked the IAU's official classification, and yes, the IAU classifies Pluto as a dwarf planet. I know some people still think of it as the ninth planet, but the official stance is clear. It's been that way since 2006, and it's still true today. The IAU defines a dwarf planet as a celestial body that orbits the sun, has enough mass for a round shape, but hasn't cleared its neighborhood. Pluto fits that perfectly. So if you're wondering, the answer is yes. I'm not making this up, it's right there on their website. Just wanted to share because I've seen a lot of confusion about this lately.

content.title: IAU still classifies Pluto as a dwarf planet, yes
content.body: I keep seeing people say Pluto was kicked out of the solar system or something, but that's not true. The International Astronomical Union officially classifies Pluto as a dwarf planet. That's the official designation, yes. It's still a planet in the dwarf category, not a full planet, but it's not just an asteroid. The IAU made this decision in 2006, and it hasn't changed.
